Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 53, verses 1–18:

Explanation of the words:

﴿By the star when it sets﴾: that is, by the Pleiades (al-Thurayya) when it sets after rising.

﴿Your companion has not strayed﴾: that is, Muhammad ﷺ has not strayed from the path of guidance.

﴿Nor has he gone astray﴾: that is, he has not been clothed in error (al-ghayy), which is ignorance arising from corrupt belief.

﴿Nor does he speak from desire﴾: that is, he does not speak from his own desire; what he says about Allah, the Exalted, does not proceed from his own whims.

﴿It is but a revelation revealed﴾: that is, it is nothing but divine revelation that is revealed to him.

﴿He was taught by one mighty in power﴾: that is, he was taught by a mighty angel, who is Jibril, peace be upon him.

﴿Possessor of strength (dhu mirrah)﴾: that is, of soundness in body and mind, and therefore possessed of great strength.

﴿Then he rose, while he was on the highest horizon﴾: that is, he settled while he was at the horizon of the sun at its rising, in the form in which Allah created him. The Prophet ﷺ saw him, and he filled the horizon up to the west. It was the Prophet ﷺ who asked Jibril to show him himself in the form in which Allah created him.

﴿Then he approached and descended﴾: that is, he drew near and descended, meaning he increased in nearness.

﴿And was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer﴾: that is, he was at a nearness equal to the measure of two bows.

﴿So He revealed to His servant what He revealed﴾: that is, Allah revealed to His servant Jibril what Jibril then revealed to the Prophet ﷺ.

﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾: that is, the heart of the Prophet did not lie about what he saw with his eyes of the form of Jibril, peace be upon him.

﴿Will you then dispute with him about what he sees?﴾: that is, will you, O polytheists, argue with him and contend with him about what he sees of Jibril's form?

﴿And he certainly saw him in another descent﴾: that is, in his form once more, and that was in the heavens on the night of the Isra'.

﴿At the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary﴾: it is a lote tree (nabq) on the right of the Throne, which none of the angels may pass beyond.

﴿Near it is the Garden of Refuge﴾: that is, the garden where the angels and the spirits of the martyrs and the righteous, the friends of Allah, take refuge.

﴿When there covered the lote-tree that which covered it﴾: that is, of the light of Allah, the Exalted, that which covered it.

﴿The sight did not swerve, nor did it transgress﴾: that is, the sight of Muhammad did not incline to the right or the left, nor did it rise beyond the limit set for it.

﴿He had certainly seen of the greatest signs of his Lord﴾: that is, he saw Jibril in his form, and he saw a green canopy (rafraf) that filled the horizon of the sky, and he saw of the wonders of Allah's creation and the manifestations of His power and knowledge what cannot be grasped or described.

Meaning of the verses:

The statement of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿By the star﴾ up to ﴿the greatest of the signs of his Lord﴾ establishes the prophethood of Muhammad, His servant and messenger ﷺ. He swears by the star when it sets, which is the star of the Pleiades when it disappears from the horizon, that Muhammad, the companion of Quraysh, has not strayed. He has been in their company since his birth, and he has not been absent from them nor they from him for a period exceeding forty years; this is complete companionship. He has not strayed from the path of guidance, and they know this. Nor has he gone astray in any way at all, nor has ignorance clung to him in word or deed so that he erred through it.

Nor does he speak of the Qur'an or anything else he says and calls to from his own desire, as may happen with other human beings. ﴿It is but a revelation revealed﴾: that is, what he speaks, calls to, and acts upon is nothing but a revelation revealed to him. ﴿He was taught by one mighty in power﴾, that is, of soundness of mind and body, and thereby he was strong in spirit, intellect and essence; this is Jibril, peace be upon him. As for His saying ﴿Then he rose﴾, it refers to Jibril, ﴿while he was on the highest horizon﴾, and the meaning of "rose" is that he settled. ﴿Then he approached and descended﴾: that is, he descended and drew near gradually until he was, from the Messenger ﷺ, at a distance of two bow-lengths; the bow is well known as an instrument for shooting. ﴿Or closer﴾: that is, than two bow-lengths.

As for His saying ﴿So He revealed to His servant what He revealed﴾: that is, Allah, the Exalted, revealed to Jibril what he then revealed to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. His saying ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾: that is, the heart of Muhammad ﷺ did not lie about what Muhammad saw with his eyes, namely Jibril in the form in which Allah, the Exalted, created him, with six hundred wings, the length of each wing being the distance between east and west. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Will you then dispute with him about what he sees?﴾ This is addressed to the polytheists who deny the Prophet's sight; Allah, the Exalted, rebukes them with His words ﴿Will you then dispute with him﴾, that is, will you contend and argue with him, O polytheists, about what he sees with his eyes. ﴿And he certainly saw him in another descent﴾: that is, once more, ﴿at the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary﴾, and that was the night he was taken on the Isra'. This lote tree is described as having leaves like the ears of elephants and fruit like the jars of Hajar; it is said that when there covered it what Allah covered it with, it changed, so that no one of Allah's creation can describe its beauty. It is called the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary because the knowledge of every knower among creation ends at it, or because it is on the right of the Throne, which none of the angels may pass beyond. His saying ﴿Near it is the Garden of Refuge﴾: that is, the garden where the angels and the spirits of the martyrs and the righteous, the friends of Allah, take refuge.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When there covered the lote-tree that which covered it﴾: that is, of the light of Allah, and the angels, out of love for Allah, were like crows leaping upon trees; thus related Ibn Jarir al-Tabari. His saying ﴿The sight did not swerve, nor did it transgress﴾: that is, the sight of Muhammad did not incline to the right or the left, nor did it rise beyond the limit set for it. ﴿He had certainly seen of the greatest signs of his Lord﴾: that is, he saw Jibril in his created form, which he has in the heavens, and he saw a green canopy that filled the horizon of the sky, and he saw of the wonders of Allah's creation and the manifestations of His power and knowledge what there is no way to grasp or speak of.

Guidance from the verses:

1. Establishing the prophethood of Muhammad and affirming it with what leaves no room for doubt or dispute.
2. Declaring the Messenger ﷺ free from speaking from desire, or from any of his deeds or words proceeding from following whim.
3. Description of Jibril, peace be upon him.
4. Affirmation that the Prophet ﷺ saw Jibril in his form as it is in the heavens, twice.
5. Establishing the event of the Isra' and Mi'raj for the Prophet ﷺ.
6. Explanation of the reality of the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 53, verses 19–26:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza﴾: That is, tell me about your idols, for whom you derived names from the names of Allah and made them feminine.

﴿And Manat, the third, the other﴾: And you made them daughters of Allah, a fabrication against Allah and a lie about Him.

﴿Is the male for you and the female for Him?﴾: That is, do you claim that you have the male, which you are pleased with for yourselves, while Allah has the female, which you are not pleased with for yourselves?

﴿That, then, is an unjust division﴾: That is, this division of yours is unjust, unfair, deficient and incomplete.

﴿They are not but names you have named﴾: That is, al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat, the third, the other, are only names with no reality behind them.

﴿You and your fathers﴾: That is, you and your fathers named them with these names.

﴿Allah has not sent down any authority for them﴾: That is, Allah the Exalted has not sent down any revelation permitting their worship.

﴿They follow nothing but assumption﴾: That is, the polytheists who worship their idols follow nothing but assumption, conjecture and falsehood.

﴿And what the souls desire﴾: That is, they follow only what their souls desire and what their appetites incline them toward.

﴿Or does man have whatever he wishes?﴾: That is, rather, does man have whatever he wishes? The answer is no, man does not have whatever he wishes.

﴿To Allah belongs the Hereafter and the first (life)﴾: That is, both the Hereafter and this world belong to Allah; He gives from them whatever He wills to whomever He wills.

﴿And how many an angel is there in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all﴾: That is, many of the angels in the heavens, even if they wished to intercede for someone, their intercession would be of no avail, unless Allah has permitted them and is pleased with the one for whom intercession is granted.

Meaning of the verses:

After Allah, the Exalted, mentioned the manifestations of His power, greatness, knowledge and wisdom in the highest realm, Gabriel, the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary, the light of Allah that covered it, and the great signs He showed His Messenger, He addressed the polytheists saying, ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza and Manat, the third, the other?﴾ That is, have you blinded yourselves so that you see these idols as worthy of being equated with the One who possesses the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and you worship them alongside Him despite their worthlessness and baseness? You increased in blindness and derived names for them from the names of Allah: from "al-'Aziz" (the Mighty) you derived "al-'Uzza," and from "Allah" you derived "al-Lat." You made them daughters of Allah, a fabrication against Allah, by your claim that they intercede for you with Allah. Tell me: is the male for you, because you love males and are pleased with them for yourselves, and the female for Him, because you dislike females and are not pleased with them for yourselves? If the matter is as you see it, then it is an unjust division, unfair and deficient, incomplete. How, then, do you assign it to Him, when you worship idols in order to draw near to Him through them so that He may fulfill your needs? ﴿They are not but names you have named, you and your fathers.﴾ Your idols, O polytheists, are nothing more than names for gods that have no existence and no reality in the world of fact, since there is no god but Allah. As for al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat, the third, the other, they were never gods that give life and cause death, bestow and withhold, harm and benefit. ﴿They are not but names you have named, you and your fathers; Allah has not sent down any authority for them,﴾ that is, He has not sent down any revelation permitting their worship.

Here the Majestic, may His majesty be exalted, turned His address away from them and said, ﴿They follow nothing but assumption,﴾ that is, these polytheists follow in the worship of these idols nothing but assumption, so they have no certainty about the correctness of worshipping them, just as they follow in their worship ﴿what the souls desire,﴾ that is, the desire of their own selves. ﴿And there has certainly come to them from their Lord guidance,﴾ which made clear to them the straight path, but they turned away from it, though it is the truth from their Lord. They clung instead to false wishes, that their idols would intercede for them. ﴿Or does man have whatever he wishes?﴾ The answer is no, he does not have whatever he wishes, since to Allah belong the Hereafter and the first life; He gives from them what He wills and withholds what He wills. ﴿And how many an angel is there in the heavens﴾ whose number is too great to count, ﴿whose intercession will not avail at all,﴾ not even slightly, ﴿unless after Allah has given permission to whom He wills to intercede, from among the angels and others, and is pleased with the one for whom intercession is made.* Otherwise, there is no intercessor and no intercession that benefits with Allah, the King, the Manifest Truth.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Condemnation of association (shirk) and the polytheists, and ridicule of their intellects for worshipping names that have no referents outside; for calling a stone a god does not make it a god.

2- Clarification that polytheists in every time and place follow nothing in the worship of other than Allah except their own desires.

3- Clarification that man is not given by his wishes, but by his deeds, sincerity and effort.

4- Clarification that the world and the Hereafter belong to Allah, so nothing from them should be sought except from Allah, their Owner.

5- Every intercession that is hoped for achieves nothing unless two conditions are met: first, that Allah permits the intercessor to intercede, and second, that Allah is pleased with the one for whom intercession is made. The summary: permission for the intercessor and approval of the one interceded for.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 53, verses 27–30:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*"Inna alladhina la yu'minuna bil-akhirah"* (Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter): that is, those who do not believe in the resurrection and the life to come.

*"Layusammuna al-malaikata tasmiyata al-untha"* (They surely name the angels with the names of females): that is, they apply female names to the angels, since they say they are daughters of God.

*"Wa ma lahum bihi min 'ilm"* (And they have no knowledge of it): that is, they have no knowledge of this from any Book, nor guidance from any Prophet, nor any reasoning.

*"In yattabi'una illa al-zann"* (They follow nothing but conjecture): that is, in their naming of the angels as females they follow nothing but mere conjecture, and conjecture establishes no proof and grants no right.

*"Fa-a'rid 'an man tawalla 'an dhikrina"* (So turn away from those who turn away from Our remembrance): that is, from the Qur'an and Our worship.

*"Wa lam yurid illa al-hayat al-dunya"* (And he desires nothing but the life of this world): and he does not intend, in his speech or his action, anything but what fulfils his worldly desires.

*"Dhalika mablaghuhum min al-'ilm"* (That is the extent of their knowledge): that is, this pursuit of the world is the limit of their knowledge, since they have preferred the world over the Hereafter.

**Meaning of the verses:**

When the Exalted condemned the polytheists, who made idols, illusions and wishful fancies into gods, and disputed and fought on their behalf, He mentioned what causes that confusion and misguidance, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter﴾, the abode of true happiness or misery, ﴿surely name the angels with the names of females﴾. Had they believed in the Hereafter, they would not have named the angels daughters of God, because the believer in the Hereafter holds himself accountable for every word and deed, having a responsibility for which he fears being called to account. By contrast, one who does not believe in the Hereafter says and does whatever he wishes, having no sense of the responsibility for which he may be held to account, and so he is destroyed and fears nothing. This is a sound and wise explanation.

As for His saying ﴿And they have no knowledge of it﴾: that is, in their claim that the angels are daughters of God, they have no knowledge worth considering. ﴿They follow nothing but conjecture, and conjecture avails nothing against the truth.﴾ On this basis, God commanded His Messenger to turn away from those among them who turned away from the truth after knowing it and from guidance after witnessing it. Thus He said: ﴿So turn away from those who turn away from Our remembrance﴾, that is, the Qur'an, the faith, the monotheism and the obedience. ﴿And he desires nothing but the life of this world﴾ in his speech, his action and his belief, since he does not believe in the Hereafter; therefore he has shaped his life according to the measure of this world, all his thinking is for the world and all his action is for it, and thus he becomes more like a machine than a living being. Life with him becomes barren of benefit, and therefore he must be turned away from and left alone until God permits something concerning him.

As for His saying ﴿That is the extent of their knowledge﴾: that is, this pursuit of the world is where their knowledge ends, and therefore they have preferred it over the Hereafter, of which they know nothing.

As for His address to His Messenger: ﴿Indeed your Lord knows best who strays from His way, and He knows best who is guided﴾: that is, your Lord, O Messenger, knows better than you and better than anyone else who has strayed from His path in decree and in fact, who has strayed in this worldly life too, and He knows who is guided, in decree and in actuality in this worldly life. He will recompense each one for what they have done, whether good or evil. So do not despair, O Our Messenger, and do not grieve, but entrust the matter to Us, for We know and We recompense every doer for what he has done in the abode of recompense.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Most diseases of the heart stem from a heart that does not believe in the Hereafter.
2. Most corruption on earth is the result of ignorance and the lack of certain knowledge.
3. A warning against the materialists, for they are evil and dangerous, and it is obligatory to turn away from them because they are the worst of creation.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 53, verses 31–32:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Wa-lillahi ma fi as-samawati wa-ma fi al-ard﴾: that is, creation, dominion and disposal.

﴿Li-yajzia alladhina asa'u bi-ma 'amilu﴾: that He may punish those who did evil with what they did, namely the shirk and sins they committed.

﴿Wa-yajzia alladhina ahsanu bi-al-husna﴾: and He will reward those who did good in their faith and righteous deeds with Paradise.

﴿Alladhina yajtanibuna kaba'ira al-ithm﴾: that is, they avoid the major sins, which are every sin for which a legal penalty (hadd) has been prescribed, or whose doer has been cursed, or which has been threatened with punishment in the Hereafter.

﴿Wa-al-fawahisha illa al-lamam﴾: that is, the vile sins such as adultery, sodomy, slander of chaste women, and stinginess. Al-lamam are the minor sins which are expiated by avoiding the major ones.

﴿Huwa a'lamu bikum idh ansha'akum mina al-ard﴾: that is, He created your father Adam from the dust of the earth.

﴿Wa-idh antum ajinnatun fi butuni ummahatikum﴾: that is, while you were in the wombs of your mothers, not yet born.

﴿Fa-la tuzakku anfusakum﴾: that is, do not praise yourselves out of boasting and self-admiration.

﴿Huwa a'lamu bi-man ittaqa﴾: that is, He knows best who among you is God-fearing and who is a sinner, so there is no need for you to mention that about yourselves.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to establish His absolute lordship over everything. Earlier in the context is His saying: ﴿So to Allah belong the Hereafter and the first life﴾ [Verse 25]. Here the Mighty One says: ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, in creation, dominion, disposal and management. So He guides whom He wills and misleads whom He wills, a guidance that follows wisdom, and a misguidance likewise. This is indicated by His saying: ﴿That He may recompense those who did evil﴾, that is, to their own detriment, ﴿with what they did of shirk and sins, He will recompense them with evil, which is Hell﴾. ﴿And recompense those who did good﴾, to their own benefit, by purifying and cleansing themselves through faith and righteous deeds, ﴿He will recompense them with the best, which is Paradise.﴾ His saying ﴿Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities﴾ shows the aspect of the goodness of the good-doers toward themselves, when they purified themselves through faith and righteous deeds and did not soil themselves with the filth of major sins, from everything whose doer is threatened with the Fire, or with a curse, or with the enforcement of a legal penalty, or with the anger of the Lord.

Immoralities include adultery, sodomy and stinginess. His saying ﴿except for the lamam. Indeed your Lord is vast in forgiveness﴾ means: but the lamam is forgiven. It is what a person commits and then repents of, or what he committed in the Jahiliyyah and then embraced Islam, and what is among minor sins such as a glance, a word, or a date (kiss). It has been explained by the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: «Allah has prescribed for the son of Adam his share of adultery, which he will inevitably encounter. The adultery of the eyes is looking, the adultery of the tongue is speech, the soul wishes and desires, and the private part either confirms that or denies it.» So the forgiveness of Allah is vast, encompassing every sin for which its doer repents, as well as every minor sin.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He knows you best, since He produced you from the earth and when you were embryos in the wombs of your mothers﴾: He knows our weakness, our instincts, our needs and our incapacity better than we ourselves do. Therefore He has overlooked for us the lamam which we commit by reason of incapacity and weakness. So to Him belong praise and grace. His saying ﴿So do not justify yourselves﴾ forbids the Lord, Exalted is He, His believing servants from declaring themselves pure by claiming perfection and cleanliness, which becomes boasting and self-admiration. Self-admiration nullifies deeds, like showing off and shirk. So His saying ﴿So do not justify yourselves﴾ means: do not testify about yourselves that you are pure and free from sins and transgressions. His saying ﴿He knows best who is God-fearing﴾ means: Allah knows best which of you fears his Lord, fears His punishment, performs the obligations and avoids the prohibitions, among us, and the God-fearing person himself. Therefore do not praise yourselves before Him, for He knows you better than you know yourselves.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Affirmation of Allah's lordship over everything, which entails His divinity.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 53, verses 31–32:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Wa-lillahi ma fi as-samawati wa-ma fi al-ard﴾: that is, creation, dominion and disposal.

﴿Li-yajzia alladhina asa'u bi-ma 'amilu﴾: that He may punish those who did evil with what they did, namely the shirk and sins they committed.

﴿Wa-yajzia alladhina ahsanu bi-al-husna﴾: and He will reward those who did good in their faith and righteous deeds with Paradise.

﴿Alladhina yajtanibuna kaba'ira al-ithm﴾: that is, they avoid the major sins, which are every sin for which a legal penalty (hadd) has been prescribed, or whose doer has been cursed, or which has been threatened with punishment in the Hereafter.

﴿Wa-al-fawahisha illa al-lamam﴾: that is, the vile sins such as adultery, sodomy, slander of chaste women, and stinginess. Al-lamam are the minor sins which are expiated by avoiding the major ones.

﴿Huwa a'lamu bikum idh ansha'akum mina al-ard﴾: that is, He created your father Adam from the dust of the earth.

﴿Wa-idh antum ajinnatun fi butuni ummahatikum﴾: that is, while you were in the wombs of your mothers, not yet born.

﴿Fa-la tuzakku anfusakum﴾: that is, do not praise yourselves out of boasting and self-admiration.

﴿Huwa a'lamu bi-man ittaqa﴾: that is, He knows best who among you is God-fearing and who is a sinner, so there is no need for you to mention that about yourselves.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to establish His absolute lordship over everything. Earlier in the context is His saying: ﴿So to Allah belong the Hereafter and the first life﴾ [Verse 25]. Here the Mighty One says: ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, in creation, dominion, disposal and management. So He guides whom He wills and misleads whom He wills, a guidance that follows wisdom, and a misguidance likewise. This is indicated by His saying: ﴿That He may recompense those who did evil﴾, that is, to their own detriment, ﴿with what they did of shirk and sins, He will recompense them with evil, which is Hell﴾. ﴿And recompense those who did good﴾, to their own benefit, by purifying and cleansing themselves through faith and righteous deeds, ﴿He will recompense them with the best, which is Paradise.﴾ His saying ﴿Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities﴾ shows the aspect of the goodness of the good-doers toward themselves, when they purified themselves through faith and righteous deeds and did not soil themselves with the filth of major sins, from everything whose doer is threatened with the Fire, or with a curse, or with the enforcement of a legal penalty, or with the anger of the Lord.

Immoralities include adultery, sodomy and stinginess. His saying ﴿except for the lamam. Indeed your Lord is vast in forgiveness﴾ means: but the lamam is forgiven. It is what a person commits and then repents of, or what he committed in the Jahiliyyah and then embraced Islam, and what is among minor sins such as a glance, a word, or a date (kiss). It has been explained by the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: «Allah has prescribed for the son of Adam his share of adultery, which he will inevitably encounter. The adultery of the eyes is looking, the adultery of the tongue is speech, the soul wishes and desires, and the private part either confirms that or denies it.» So the forgiveness of Allah is vast, encompassing every sin for which its doer repents, as well as every minor sin.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He knows you best, since He produced you from the earth and when you were embryos in the wombs of your mothers﴾: He knows our weakness, our instincts, our needs and our incapacity better than we ourselves do. Therefore He has overlooked for us the lamam which we commit by reason of incapacity and weakness. So to Him belong praise and grace. His saying ﴿So do not justify yourselves﴾ forbids the Lord, Exalted is He, His believing servants from declaring themselves pure by claiming perfection and cleanliness, which becomes boasting and self-admiration. Self-admiration nullifies deeds, like showing off and shirk. So His saying ﴿So do not justify yourselves﴾ means: do not testify about yourselves that you are pure and free from sins and transgressions. His saying ﴿He knows best who is God-fearing﴾ means: Allah knows best which of you fears his Lord, fears His punishment, performs the obligations and avoids the prohibitions, among us, and the God-fearing person himself. Therefore do not praise yourselves before Him, for He knows you better than you know yourselves.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 53, verses 33–54:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Have you seen the one who turned away﴾: i.e., from Islam, after he had almost entered it.

﴿Gave a little and then stopped short﴾: i.e., he gave the one who claimed he would bear his punishment in the Hereafter what he had promised him of wealth, and then withheld it.

﴿Does he have knowledge of the unseen so that he sees?﴾: i.e., does he know that another will bear his punishment? The answer is no.

﴿Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham, who fulfilled [his covenant]?﴾: i.e., rather, he has not been informed of what was revealed in the aforementioned scriptures, namely the Torah and the ten scrolls that were given to Abraham, peace be upon him.

﴿That no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾: i.e., no sinful soul will carry the sin of another.

﴿And that there is not for man except what he strives for﴾: i.e., [what he earns] of good and evil; he has neither the reward nor the burden of another's striving.

﴿And that his effort will be seen﴾: i.e., it will be made visible on the Day of Resurrection, and he will see it himself.

﴿Then he will be recompensed with the fullest recompense﴾: i.e., the most complete and perfect, lacking nothing.

﴿That to your Lord is the finality﴾: i.e., the return and the destination; to Him the affairs of His servants ultimately lead after death, and He will repay them.

﴿And that it is He who causes laughter and causes weeping﴾: i.e., He makes whom He wills joyful, so he laughs, and makes whom He wills sad, so he weeps.

﴿And that it is He who causes death and gives life﴾: He causes death in this world and gives life in the Hereafter.

﴿And that He created the pairs, male and female﴾: i.e., the two kinds, male and female.

﴿From a sperm-drop when it is emitted﴾: i.e., from semen when it is poured into the womb.

﴿And that upon Him is the other creation﴾: i.e., the second creation for resurrection and recompense.

﴿And that it is He who enriches and suffices﴾: i.e., He alone enriched some people with sufficiency, and gave others wealth to keep and store.

﴿And that He is the Lord of Sirius﴾: i.e., its Creator and Owner; it is a star that rises after Orion, which the polytheists worshipped.

﴿And that He destroyed the former ʿĀd﴾: i.e., the people of Hud, peace be upon him.

﴿And Thamud, so He left none﴾: i.e., He destroyed them too, and none of them remained; they were the people of Salih.

﴿And the people of Noah before them﴾: i.e., He destroyed the people of Noah before ʿĀd and Thamud, and the people of Lot.

﴿And the overturned cities He hurled down﴾: i.e., He cast down the cities of the people of Lot after raising them up to the sky, overturned toward the earth, since ʾiftikāk means overturning.

﴿Then covered them with that which covered﴾: i.e., with punishment that covered them, when He made their highest part their lowest and rained down upon them stones of sijjil.

Meaning of the verses:

These verses portray an ignorant Qurashi man, al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, who once listened to the recitation of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, was moved by it, and the Messenger invited him, so he embraced Islam or was about to. One of the polytheists from their devils learned of this, came to him, and reproached him for accepting Islam and abandoning the religion of his forefathers. Al-Walid excused himself, saying that he feared the punishment of Allah. The Qurashi devil, who was poor while al-Walid was rich, said to him: "Give me such-and-such an amount of wealth monthly, weekly, or yearly, and I will bear your punishment that you fear. Return to your religion and remain upon it." Al-Walid agreed to the offer and began giving him money. Then he "stopped short," meaning he cut off what he had been giving and withheld it.

Allah the Exalted revealed these verses concerning him as consolation for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and as instruction and warning for everyone to whom they reach, who recites them or has them recited to him. He said, in a style that stirs the listener to wonder: ﴿Have you seen the one who turned away﴾, i.e., from Islam after he had nearly reached it and entered it. ﴿And gave a little﴾, i.e., of wealth, to the polytheist devil with whom he agreed that he would bear his punishment in exchange for wealth he would give him in installments, ﴿and stopped short﴾, i.e., he cut off and withheld. A digger who digs a well in the ground sometimes encounters a hard rock of solid earth, is unable to dig further, stops digging and desists; likewise al-Walid gave, then withheld, and this is the meaning of akda, i.e., he came upon hard earth.

As for His saying: ﴿Does he have knowledge of the unseen so that he sees?﴾, i.e., could a person bear the punishment of another on the Day of Resurrection? The answer is no. He has no knowledge of the unseen, neither from a Book nor from a Sunnah. ﴿Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Moses, which is the Torah, and of Abraham, who fulfilled [his covenant] to his Lord in all that was enjoined upon him, such as sacrificing his son, when he laid him down on his forehead to slaughter him, and building the House, emigrating, circumcision by the adze, and other arduous obligations?⁠ That is, has this ignorant man not been informed, i.e., told, of what is in the scriptures of Moses son of ʿImran, prophet of the Children of Israel, and Abraham, father of the prophets? Then Allah the Exalted explained what those scriptures contained of knowledge, saying:

﴿That no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾: that no sinful soul will bear the sin of another soul.

﴿And that there is not for man any reward on the Day of Resurrection except what he strove to attain himself.⁠ This does not contradict the saying of the Messenger ﷺ in the Sahih: "When the son of Adam dies, his deeds end except for three: a righteous child who prays for him, ongoing charity, or knowledge from which people benefit," for these three are matters of a person's own work and striving: the child he begot and raised, the ongoing charity he endowed himself, and the knowledge he learned and spread among people and taught. All of them are from his striving and earnings.

﴿And that his striving, i.e., his deeds in this world, good or evil, will be seen openly and he will be recompensed for it, whether good or evil. ﴿The fullest recompense﴾, i.e., the most complete and perfect.

﴿And that to your Lord is the finality﴾, i.e., to Him the affairs of His servants return after death, and He judges them and repays them for them.

﴿And that it is He who causes laughter and causes weeping﴾, i.e., He makes whom He wills joyful and saddens whom He wills; joy produces laughter and sorrow produces weeping. He made the people of Paradise laugh and the people of the Fire weep, in addition to those He made joyful or saddened in this world.

﴿And that it is He who causes death and gives life﴾: He causes death at the end of a servant's term and gives him life in his grave and on the day of resurrection and gathering; He gives life through faith and causes death through disbelief; He causes death through drought and gives life through rain.

﴿And that He created the pairs﴾, i.e., the two kinds, male and female, among all animals, ﴿from a sperm-drop when it is emitted﴾, i.e., a drop of semen, when it is poured into the wombs.

﴿And that upon Him, exalted is He, is the other creation﴾, i.e., He is the One who undertakes it, reviving the creatures after their death on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿And that it is He who enriches and suffices﴾, i.e., He enriched some people, meeting their needs and sparing them their burdens, and gave others abundant wealth which they kept and stored.

﴿And that He is the Lord of Sirius﴾, that star which rises after Orion. Allah is its Creator, Owner, and Subjugator, yet the ignorant worshipped it and took it as a lord and god, though it is itself a created, owned, and worshipped thing.

﴿And that He destroyed the former ʿĀd﴾, the people of Hud. He sent upon them a violent wind which left nothing it touched but made it like crumbled dust. ʿĀd, that nation which said, "Who is stronger than us?" Allah destroyed them and annihilated them all.

﴿And Thamud, so He left none﴾, i.e., He destroyed Thamud, the people of Salih, with the Cry, and left none of them remaining.

﴿And the people of Noah before them, [He destroyed them] because they were more unjust and more rebellious than the others.

﴿And the overturned cities﴾, i.e., the cities of the people of Lot, Sodom and Gomorrah. He destroyed them: He raised those cities up to the height of the sky, then hurled them down to the earth, and sent upon them stones of clay, of sijjil, so that the painful punishment covered those cities, a punishment beyond the power of description. This is Allah, Lord of the worlds, whom the ignorant took as equals and worshipped alongside Him.

This is Allah, the true God, whom people have taken besides Him as gods that know not, judge not, and have no power.

This is Allah, the Mighty, the Avenger on behalf of His friends against His enemies; He makes wretched the servant who opposes Him and makes happy the one who allies with Him.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Affirmation of the Lordship of Allah the Exalted and establishment of His divinity through proofs and arguments that can in no way be refuted.

2- Affirmation of the justice of Allah the Exalted in His judgment and decree.

3- Manifestations of the power, knowledge, and wisdom of Allah the Exalted.

4- Establishment of a factual truth: that the deed which purifies the soul or defiles it is the one a person performs himself, by his own choice, intention, and purpose.

5- A warning to the oppressors and tyrants among the people of disbelief and polytheism that they may suffer what befell others of ruin and loss.

﴿Have you seen the one who turned away﴾: i.e., from Islam, after he had almost entered it.

﴿Gave a little and then stopped short﴾: i.e., he gave the one who claimed he would bear his punishment in the Hereafter what he had promised him of wealth, and then withheld it.

﴿Does he have knowledge of the unseen so that he sees?﴾: i.e., does he know that another will bear his punishment? The answer is no.

﴿Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham, who fulfilled [his covenant]?﴾: i.e., rather, he has not been informed of what was revealed in the aforementioned scriptures, namely the Torah and the ten scrolls that were given to Abraham, peace be upon him.

﴿That no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾: i.e., no sinful soul will carry the sin of another.

﴿And that there is not for man except what he strives for﴾: i.e., [what he earns] of good and evil; he has neither the reward nor the burden of another's striving.

﴿And that his effort will be seen﴾: i.e., it will be made visible on the Day of Resurrection, and he will see it himself.

﴿Then he will be recompensed with the fullest recompense﴾: i.e., the most complete and perfect, lacking nothing.

﴿That to your Lord is the finality﴾: i.e., the return and the destination; to Him the affairs of His servants ultimately lead after death, and He will repay them.

﴿And that it is He who causes laughter and causes weeping﴾: i.e., He makes whom He wills joyful, so he laughs, and makes whom He wills sad, so he weeps.

﴿And that it is He who causes death and gives life﴾: He causes death in this world and gives life in the Hereafter.

﴿And that He created the pairs, male and female﴾: i.e., the two kinds, male and female.

﴿From a sperm-drop when it is emitted﴾: i.e., from semen when it is poured into the womb.

﴿And that upon Him is the other creation﴾: i.e., the second creation for resurrection and recompense.

﴿And that it is He who enriches and suffices﴾: i.e., He alone enriched some people with sufficiency, and gave others wealth to keep and store.

﴿And that He is the Lord of Sirius﴾: i.e., its Creator and Owner; it is a star that rises after Orion, which the polytheists worshipped.

﴿And that He destroyed the former ʿĀd﴾: i.e., the people of Hud, peace be upon him.

﴿And Thamud, so He left none﴾: i.e., He destroyed them too, and none of them remained; they were the people of Salih.

﴿And the people of Noah before them﴾: i.e., He destroyed the people of Noah before ʿĀd and Thamud, and the people of Lot.

﴿And the overturned cities He hurled down﴾: i.e., He cast down the cities of the people of Lot after raising them up to the sky, overturned toward the earth, since ʾiftikāk means overturning.

﴿Then covered them with that which covered﴾: i.e., with punishment that covered them, when He made their highest part their lowest and rained down upon them stones of sijjil.

Meaning of the verses:

These verses portray an ignorant Qurashi man, al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, who once listened to the recitation of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, was moved by it, and the Messenger invited him, so he embraced Islam or was about to. One of the polytheists from their devils learned of this, came to him, and reproached him for accepting Islam and abandoning the religion of his forefathers. Al-Walid excused himself, saying that he feared the punishment of Allah. The Qurashi devil, who was poor while al-Walid was rich, said to him: "Give me such-and-such an amount of wealth monthly, weekly, or yearly, and I will bear your punishment that you fear. Return to your religion and remain upon it." Al-Walid agreed to the offer and began giving him money. Then he "stopped short," meaning he cut off what he had been giving and withheld it.

Allah the Exalted revealed these verses concerning him as consolation for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and as instruction and warning for everyone to whom they reach, who recites them or has them recited to him. He said, in a style that stirs the listener to wonder: ﴿Have you seen the one who turned away﴾, i.e., from Islam after he had nearly reached it and entered it. ﴿And gave a little﴾, i.e., of wealth, to the polytheist devil with whom he agreed that he would bear his punishment in exchange for wealth he would give him in installments, ﴿and stopped short﴾, i.e., he cut off and withheld. A digger who digs a well in the ground sometimes encounters a hard rock of solid earth, is unable to dig further, stops digging and desists; likewise al-Walid gave, then withheld, and this is the meaning of akda, i.e., he came upon hard earth.

As for His saying: ﴿Does he have knowledge of the unseen so that he sees?﴾, i.e., could a person bear the punishment of another on the Day of Resurrection? The answer is no. He has no knowledge of the unseen, neither from a Book nor from a Sunnah. ﴿Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Moses, which is the Torah, and of Abraham, who fulfilled [his covenant] to his Lord in all that was enjoined upon him, such as sacrificing his son, when he laid him down on his forehead to slaughter him, and building the House, emigrating, circumcision by the adze, and other arduous obligations?⁠ That is, has this ignorant man not been informed, i.e., told, of what is in the scriptures of Moses son of ʿImran, prophet of the Children of Israel, and Abraham, father of the prophets? Then Allah the Exalted explained what those scriptures contained of knowledge, saying:

﴿That no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾: that no sinful soul will bear the sin of another soul.

﴿And that there is not for man any reward on the Day of Resurrection except what he strove to attain himself.⁠ This does not contradict the saying of the Messenger ﷺ in the Sahih: "When the son of Adam dies, his deeds end except for three: a righteous child who prays for him, ongoing charity, or knowledge from which people benefit," for these three are matters of a person's own work and striving: the child he begot and raised, the ongoing charity he endowed himself, and the knowledge he learned and spread among people and taught. All of them are from his striving and earnings.

﴿And that his striving, i.e., his deeds in this world, good or evil, will be seen openly and he will be recompensed for it, whether good or evil. ﴿The fullest recompense﴾, i.e., the most complete and perfect.

﴿And that to your Lord is the finality﴾, i.e., to Him the affairs of His servants return after death, and He judges them and repays them for them.

﴿And that it is He who causes laughter and causes weeping﴾, i.e., He makes whom He wills joyful and saddens whom He wills; joy produces laughter and sorrow produces weeping. He made the people of Paradise laugh and the people of the Fire weep, in addition to those He made joyful or saddened in this world.

﴿And that it is He who causes death and gives life﴾: He causes death at the end of a servant's term and gives him life in his grave and on the day of resurrection and gathering; He gives life through faith and causes death through disbelief; He causes death through drought and gives life through rain.

﴿And that He created the pairs﴾, i.e., the two kinds, male and female, among all animals, ﴿from a sperm-drop when it is emitted﴾, i.e., a drop of semen, when it is poured into the wombs.

﴿And that upon Him, exalted is He, is the other creation﴾, i.e., He is the One who undertakes it, reviving the creatures after their death on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿And that it is He who enriches and suffices﴾, i.e., He enriched some people, meeting their needs and sparing them their burdens, and gave others abundant wealth which they kept and stored.

﴿And that He is the Lord of Sirius﴾, that star which rises after Orion. Allah is its Creator, Owner, and Subjugator, yet the ignorant worshipped it and took it as a lord and god, though it is itself a created, owned, and worshipped thing.

﴿And that He destroyed the former ʿĀd﴾, the people of Hud. He sent upon them a violent wind which left nothing it touched but made it like crumbled dust. ʿĀd, that nation which said, "Who is stronger than us?" Allah destroyed them and annihilated them all.

﴿And Thamud, so He left none﴾, i.e., He destroyed Thamud, the people of Salih, with the Cry, and left none of them remaining.

﴿And the people of Noah before them, [He destroyed them] because they were more unjust and more rebellious than the others.

﴿And the overturned cities﴾, i.e., the cities of the people of Lot, Sodom and Gomorrah. He destroyed them: He raised those cities up to the height of the sky, then hurled them down to the earth, and sent upon them stones of clay, of sijjil, so that the painful punishment covered those cities, a punishment beyond the power of description. This is Allah, Lord of the worlds, whom the ignorant took as equals and worshipped alongside Him.

This is Allah, the true God, whom people have taken besides Him as gods that know not, judge not, and have no power.

This is Allah, the Mighty, the Avenger on behalf of His friends against His enemies; He makes wretched the servant who opposes Him and makes happy the one who allies with Him.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Affirmation of the Lordship of Allah the Exalted and establishment of His divinity through proofs and arguments that can in no way be refuted.

2- Affirmation of the justice of Allah the Exalted in His judgment and decree.

3- Manifestations of the power, knowledge, and wisdom of Allah the Exalted.

4- Establishment of a factual truth: that the deed which purifies the soul or defiles it is the one a person performs himself, by his own choice, intention, and purpose.

5- A warning to the oppressors and tyrants among the people of disbelief and polytheism that they may suffer what befell others of ruin and loss.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 53, verses 33–54:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Have you seen the one who turned away﴾: i.e., from Islam, after he had almost entered it.

﴿Gave a little and then stopped short﴾: i.e., he gave the one who claimed he would bear his punishment in the Hereafter what he had promised him of wealth, and then withheld it.

﴿Does he have knowledge of the unseen so that he sees?﴾: i.e., does he know that another will bear his punishment? The answer is no.

﴿Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham, who fulfilled [his covenant]?﴾: i.e., rather, he has not been informed of what was revealed in the aforementioned scriptures, namely the Torah and the ten scrolls that were given to Abraham, peace be upon him.

﴿That no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾: i.e., no sinful soul will carry the sin of another.

﴿And that there is not for man except what he strives for﴾: i.e., [what he earns] of good and evil; he has neither the reward nor the burden of another's striving.

﴿And that his effort will be seen﴾: i.e., it will be made visible on the Day of Resurrection, and he will see it himself.

﴿Then he will be recompensed with the fullest recompense﴾: i.e., the most complete and perfect, lacking nothing.

﴿That to your Lord is the finality﴾: i.e., the return and the destination; to Him the affairs of His servants ultimately lead after death, and He will repay them.

﴿And that it is He who causes laughter and causes weeping﴾: i.e., He makes whom He wills joyful, so he laughs, and makes whom He wills sad, so he weeps.

﴿And that it is He who causes death and gives life﴾: He causes death in this world and gives life in the Hereafter.

﴿And that He created the pairs, male and female﴾: i.e., the two kinds, male and female.

﴿From a sperm-drop when it is emitted﴾: i.e., from semen when it is poured into the womb.

﴿And that upon Him is the other creation﴾: i.e., the second creation for resurrection and recompense.

﴿And that it is He who enriches and suffices﴾: i.e., He alone enriched some people with sufficiency, and gave others wealth to keep and store.

﴿And that He is the Lord of Sirius﴾: i.e., its Creator and Owner; it is a star that rises after Orion, which the polytheists worshipped.

﴿And that He destroyed the former ʿĀd﴾: i.e., the people of Hud, peace be upon him.

﴿And Thamud, so He left none﴾: i.e., He destroyed them too, and none of them remained; they were the people of Salih.

﴿And the people of Noah before them﴾: i.e., He destroyed the people of Noah before ʿĀd and Thamud, and the people of Lot.

﴿And the overturned cities He hurled down﴾: i.e., He cast down the cities of the people of Lot after raising them up to the sky, overturned toward the earth, since ʾiftikāk means overturning.

﴿Then covered them with that which covered﴾: i.e., with punishment that covered them, when He made their highest part their lowest and rained down upon them stones of sijjil.

Meaning of the verses:

These verses portray an ignorant Qurashi man, al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, who once listened to the recitation of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, was moved by it, and the Messenger invited him, so he embraced Islam or was about to. One of the polytheists from their devils learned of this, came to him, and reproached him for accepting Islam and abandoning the religion of his forefathers. Al-Walid excused himself, saying that he feared the punishment of Allah. The Qurashi devil, who was poor while al-Walid was rich, said to him: "Give me such-and-such an amount of wealth monthly, weekly, or yearly, and I will bear your punishment that you fear. Return to your religion and remain upon it." Al-Walid agreed to the offer and began giving him money. Then he "stopped short," meaning he cut off what he had been giving and withheld it.

Allah the Exalted revealed these verses concerning him as consolation for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and as instruction and warning for everyone to whom they reach, who recites them or has them recited to him. He said, in a style that stirs the listener to wonder: ﴿Have you seen the one who turned away﴾, i.e., from Islam after he had nearly reached it and entered it. ﴿And gave a little﴾, i.e., of wealth, to the polytheist devil with whom he agreed that he would bear his punishment in exchange for wealth he would give him in installments, ﴿and stopped short﴾, i.e., he cut off and withheld. A digger who digs a well in the ground sometimes encounters a hard rock of solid earth, is unable to dig further, stops digging and desists; likewise al-Walid gave, then withheld, and this is the meaning of akda, i.e., he came upon hard earth.

As for His saying: ﴿Does he have knowledge of the unseen so that he sees?﴾, i.e., could a person bear the punishment of another on the Day of Resurrection? The answer is no. He has no knowledge of the unseen, neither from a Book nor from a Sunnah. ﴿Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Moses, which is the Torah, and of Abraham, who fulfilled [his covenant] to his Lord in all that was enjoined upon him, such as sacrificing his son, when he laid him down on his forehead to slaughter him, and building the House, emigrating, circumcision by the adze, and other arduous obligations?⁠ That is, has this ignorant man not been informed, i.e., told, of what is in the scriptures of Moses son of ʿImran, prophet of the Children of Israel, and Abraham, father of the prophets? Then Allah the Exalted explained what those scriptures contained of knowledge, saying:

﴿That no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾: that no sinful soul will bear the sin of another soul.

﴿And that there is not for man any reward on the Day of Resurrection except what he strove to attain himself.⁠ This does not contradict the saying of the Messenger ﷺ in the Sahih: "When the son of Adam dies, his deeds end except for three: a righteous child who prays for him, ongoing charity, or knowledge from which people benefit," for these three are matters of a person's own work and striving: the child he begot and raised, the ongoing charity he endowed himself, and the knowledge he learned and spread among people and taught. All of them are from his striving and earnings.

﴿And that his striving, i.e., his deeds in this world, good or evil, will be seen openly and he will be recompensed for it, whether good or evil. ﴿The fullest recompense﴾, i.e., the most complete and perfect.

﴿And that to your Lord is the finality﴾, i.e., to Him the affairs of His servants return after death, and He judges them and repays them for them.

﴿And that it is He who causes laughter and causes weeping﴾, i.e., He makes whom He wills joyful and saddens whom He wills; joy produces laughter and sorrow produces weeping. He made the people of Paradise laugh and the people of the Fire weep, in addition to those He made joyful or saddened in this world.

﴿And that it is He who causes death and gives life﴾: He causes death at the end of a servant's term and gives him life in his grave and on the day of resurrection and gathering; He gives life through faith and causes death through disbelief; He causes death through drought and gives life through rain.

﴿And that He created the pairs﴾, i.e., the two kinds, male and female, among all animals, ﴿from a sperm-drop when it is emitted﴾, i.e., a drop of semen, when it is poured into the wombs.

﴿And that upon Him, exalted is He, is the other creation﴾, i.e., He is the One who undertakes it, reviving the creatures after their death on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿And that it is He who enriches and suffices﴾, i.e., He enriched some people, meeting their needs and sparing them their burdens, and gave others abundant wealth which they kept and stored.

﴿And that He is the Lord of Sirius﴾, that star which rises after Orion. Allah is its Creator, Owner, and Subjugator, yet the ignorant worshipped it and took it as a lord and god, though it is itself a created, owned, and worshipped thing.

﴿And that He destroyed the former ʿĀd﴾, the people of Hud. He sent upon them a violent wind which left nothing it touched but made it like crumbled dust. ʿĀd, that nation which said, "Who is stronger than us?" Allah destroyed them and annihilated them all.

﴿And Thamud, so He left none﴾, i.e., He destroyed Thamud, the people of Salih, with the Cry, and left none of them remaining.

﴿And the people of Noah before them, [He destroyed them] because they were more unjust and more rebellious than the others.

﴿And the overturned cities﴾, i.e., the cities of the people of Lot, Sodom and Gomorrah. He destroyed them: He raised those cities up to the height of the sky, then hurled them down to the earth, and sent upon them stones of clay, of sijjil, so that the painful punishment covered those cities, a punishment beyond the power of description. This is Allah, Lord of the worlds, whom the ignorant took as equals and worshipped alongside Him.

This is Allah, the true God, whom people have taken besides Him as gods that know not, judge not, and have no power.

This is Allah, the Mighty, the Avenger on behalf of His friends against His enemies; He makes wretched the servant who opposes Him and makes happy the one who allies with Him.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 53, verses 55–62**

**Explanation of the words:**

**Fa-bi-ayyi ālā'i Rabbika:** That is, by which of the bounties of your Lord, upon you and upon others, O mankind.

**Tatamārā:** That is, you doubt or deny.

**Hādhā nadhīrun min al-nudhuri al-ūlā:** That is, this Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) is a warner from among the earlier warners, a messenger like the earlier messengers who were sent to their peoples.

**Azifati al-āzifah:** That is, the Hour has drawn near. It is described as near because it is indeed near.

**Laysa lahā min dūni Allāhi kāshifah:** That is, the Hour has no one, other than God, who can reveal it, who can make manifest its time, since none can disclose its time except God, glorified and exalted.

**Afa-min hādhā al-ḥadīth:** That is, the Qur'an.

**Ta'jabūna wa-tadḥakūn:** That is, you marvel at it in denial, and you laugh at it in mockery.

**Wa-antum sāmidūn:** That is, heedless, occupied with falsehood in speech, such as singing, and in action, such as worshipping idols and images.

**Fa-sjudū lillāh:** That is, to God, who created you, provided for you and sustains you, and do not prostrate to idols.

**Wa-‘budū:** That is, and humble yourselves before Him, exalting Him, loving Him and fearing Him, for He is your true God, and you have no god besides Him.

**The meaning of the verses:**

After this great presentation of the manifestations of power, knowledge and wisdom, all of which necessitate lordship and divinity for God alone, God addressed mankind, saying: ﴿So which of the bounties of your Lord will you doubt?﴾ That is, after what We have set before you in this surah of the manifestations of blessings and punishments, all of which are, in their inner reality, blessings, which of your Lord's bounties do you doubt, that is, dispute or deny? All of them stand before you, and you cannot deny or conceal them under any circumstances.

Then He said: ﴿This is a warner of the earlier warners.﴾ This refers to one of two things: either to what is in this surah and in the whole Qur'an of warnings, or to the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). Both are true: the Qur'an is a warner, and Muhammad is a warner from among the earlier warners who preceded him, namely the messengers, or what the messengers warned their peoples of, the punishment of God, swift in this world and deferred in the Hereafter. Beware, O people, of the consequences of your turning away.

As for His words: ﴿The imminent [Hour] has drawn near.﴾ God informs that the Resurrection has come near its appointed time and its hour has arrived; it is indeed very near. ﴿There is none to disclose it besides God﴾, to lift the veil from it and make it manifest. Rather, it remains hidden for a divine wisdom, so that mankind will be taken by surprise by it. ﴿And woe on that Day to the deniers.﴾

And His words, as a rebuke to the polytheists and deniers: ﴿Is it at this discourse that you marvel﴾, that is, you have become so heedless that you marvel at this divine discourse and this Lordly speech, which is the Qur'an. ﴿And you laugh﴾, as if your hearts had been struck by death. You do not weep over yourselves, though you have sold them to Satan, to bring them forward to the Fire of Hell as fuel, ﴿while you are sāmidūn﴾, heedless, playing and diverting yourselves, singing and amusing yourselves. Woe to you! Save yourselves: prostrate to God and worship Him, for there is no salvation for you from the painful punishment except by casting yourselves down before Him in submission and humility. Worship Him by affirming His oneness in worship, and surrender to Him your hearts and faces, so that you take no one but God as deity and object of worship, exalting and loving Him, and drawing near to Him by doing what He loves and abandoning what He hates.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Clarification of the nearness of the Hour and that its exact time is hidden from every creature of God, so that it comes suddenly.
2. Condemnation of laughter accompanied by immersion in desires.
3. Encouragement to weep out of fear of God.
4. Disapproval of singing, frivolity and play.
5. The legitimacy of prostrating upon reciting this verse, for the one who recites it and for the one who hears it. It is one of the obligatory prostrations (sajdat al-‘azā’im) in the noble Qur'an. Among the distinctive features of this prostration is that the polytheists prostrated along with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) around the Ka'bah, as is related in the Ṣaḥīḥ.
